headline: Kizashi is the continuative stem of the verb 兆す (kizasu, “to show signs”).
レンジ is borrowed from English range.
Ōhaba is 大 (ō-, “large”) plus 幅 (haba, “width, breadth”).
Kiryū is 気, air, plus 流, current or flow.
Tsue is from Old Japanese and is found in the Man'yōshū.
Tsukuri is the continuative stem of the verb 作る (tsukuru, “to make, to produce, to manufacture”).
Kanbu is a calque of French cadre (“executive, manager”), from 幹 (kan, “core, main part”) plus 部 (bu, “division, department”).
Mujaki is 無 (“non-”) plus 邪気 (“malice”), which occur in Classical Chinese but never as a single word.
Kerai was originally 家礼 (kerai).
ペット is borrowed from English pet, and the source also lists clippings of トランペット (toranpetto, “trumpet”) and English PET.
Menjo is borrowed from Chinese 免除 (miǎnchú).
Wara is from Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *wara.
Oteage is 御 (o, honorific prefix) plus 手 (te, “hand, hands”) plus 上げ (age, “raising”), the stem of 上げる (ageru).
In ikō, 向 is a daiyōji replacing 嚮.
Osu is 雄 (o, “male”) plus す (su), though the su is of unknown derivation.
デッサン is borrowed from French dessin (“a sketch, a drawing”).
Kogecha is 焦げる (kogeru, “to burn, to blacken”) plus 茶 (cha, “(tea) brown”).
インターチェンジ is from English interchange.
Tsuihō is a Sinicization of 追い放つ (oihanatsu).
Samo is さ (sa, “that way”) plus も (mo, “even”).
Gangu is from Middle Chinese 玩具 (MC ngwanH gjuH).
エレガント is borrowed from English elegant.
Chisei is from Middle Chinese 知性 (MC trje sjengH).
Michibiku is likely 道 (michi, “path”) plus 引く (hiku, “to pull; to draw”), meaning “to pull along a path”.
Jaku, “delicate”, is from Middle Chinese 弱 (MC nyak).
Omonzuru shifted from Classical Japanese 重んず (omonzu), from 重 (omo, stem of 重い (omoi, “heavy”)) plus み plus す, literally “to treat as heavy”.
Midareru is from Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic, and is compared with みだら (midara, “obscene, indecent”) and 乱す (midasu, “to disturb”).
Namari is perhaps related to Goguryeo 乃勿.
Kansen was coined in 1872 by Okuyama Torafumi in 医語類聚 (Igo ruiju) as a translation of English affection.
マイクロフォン is from English microphone.
Saeru is cognate with 清 (saya) and さやか (sayaka).
